tagline: Write the policy once, arm it when ready — the pack keeps it.
lore: A covenant is a binding promise — here it captures your tagging and ACR policy once, then keeps it: planning first, executing only when armed, looping every few hours.
problem: Tags and ACR go stale the moment the estate changes. The pack can find and propose all day, but if a human has to approve every tag on every cycle, upkeep stops the first busy week — and automation nobody can review is automation nobody trusts.
does: Covenant turns your tagging history and a plain-English policy into a workflow: which hounds tag, with what logic, which ACR changes to make, which stale tags to clear first, and how often to run. It always shows the plan first; only when you arm it does the loop execute — every few hours, behind the same write gate as everything else.

glance.caption: Covenant's plan preview: for each enabled hound, the tags it would apply on this cycle and how many assets each covers, followed by the ACR changes — reviewed before the Contract is armed.

capabilities: build the contract from the Tagging log (or an exported tag-log CSV): the hounds you used and the ACR changes you made become the starting policy.
19 tagging hounds, each on or off with plain-English logic; without a policy a hound proposes its riskiest top 50.
describe a calibration and Covenant writes the rule; optionally protect the changed assets with NO : UPDATE.
clear the tags you list at the top of a cycle, pause for Tenable to catch up, then re-tag — without deleting the tags themselves.
disarmed, the loop only plans; armed (with writes enabled) it runs on a schedule, every 4 hours by default. A one-off cycle runs only when you confirm it.
a QA pass on what landed, the loop log, Alert Raven's checks, and a run-summary email through Gabriel.
export the plan as a runnable navi script for when writes must run somewhere else.
how: Each cycle can kick off `navi update assets` and `vulns` in the background, builds the plan from each hound's own discovery and tag scheme (the same tags a person would apply from that hound's page), then — only if armed — runs it through the background tag queue. Contracts can be saved and loaded as JSON files.
who: Vulnerability management program owners who need upkeep to survive a busy quarter, and automation engineers who want autonomy an auditor can follow.
better: Covenant orchestrates the tagging hounds — Laelaps, Pythia, Certania, Charon, Linnaeus, Fenrir, Nemesis, Terminus and the rest — plus Anubis's ACR rules and Garmr's removals. Alert Raven's checks and Gabriel's summary ride along on every cycle.
different: each hound's adapter mirrors its own tag button — no separate automation scheme.
the loop runs only when armed, a one-off cycle only when you confirm it — both behind the write gate.
save, load or export the contract — your policy outlives the session.
cta: Write your Contract, arm it when you're ready — then read the summary, not the backlog.
